source_profile.source_title: Memory Maker · Timeworm — The Branching Archive
source_profile.core_idea: A small luminous jellyfish swims a branching deep-sea film archive. Recovered films grow into timeworm arms, and the route the swimmer chooses becomes part of the edit.
source_profile.generative_goal: Forge a playable design in which the camera leaves water ahead, films are worth stopping beside, animals alter the current, and a swimmer can make and finish a cut alone or with a partner.

riverbed.core_identity: The jelly carries film as anatomy. It navigates by reading currents and light, gathers frames through contact, and surfaces with a cut it can watch or swim again.
hinge_conditions: Keep the jelly small against the archive. The reference contact sheet supplies the scale relationship: an amber body surrounded by dark water, with enough room for a face, a hand, or a landscape to appear beside it.
Keep swimming and watching distinct but connected. Approach a film in the water, linger alongside it, and carry a frame from that encounter into the edit.
Make branches actual route choices. Each mouth shows an upcoming film or ecological cue, and each chosen branch changes which material and animals the swimmer encounters.
Give every newly recovered film one timeline arm. Later captures from that film lengthen its arm and join it in source order.
End a dive at an identifiable surface, where the player can see what was recovered and watch the result.
identity_constraints: Render moving film as Gaussian flecks or a timeworm of successive slices. Keep the source title and timestamp attached from first encounter through capture, edit, and playback.
Use a trailing camera with a level horizon while steering. A deliberate Look gesture opens an oblique side view and returns to the same trailing composition on release.

In ordinary play, target a bell width of 12–18% of the shorter viewport dimension. Keep the bell and active arm tips clear of the screen edge. As timelines accumulate, send the oldest tails into the depth of the wake.
Treat the dense fault image as a brief disturbance. Bright stock, red interference, and closely spaced fragments may surge locally before the water and silhouettes become legible again.
governing_rules: Drag in the water to steer with proportional input. Releasing the drag restores drift. Cast reaches, Focus slows the current for viewing, and Look shifts the camera. Each operation has a distinct input.
Use buoyancy, viscous drag, and gentle cross-currents. Remove outward velocity at a wall so the jelly slides along it and can steer away.
Preview a branch before its commitment point. Commit only after the swimmer crosses its throat, and provide a downstream rejoin or a marked return eddy.
Let creatures change local conditions through visible motion. Shrimp disturb particles, comb jellies trace currents, rays pull a broad wake, and an anglerfish changes the cost of lingering.
Treat cooperation as optional. A second swimmer may illuminate an adjacent slice or share a captured frame. Every route and objective remains achievable alone.
continuity_anchors: Track the same amber bell, current direction, and recovered film arms through every camera move.
Carry the same film and playback timestamp from an in-water screening into the Screening Room.
Keep the swimmer marker, chosen route, and nearby fork aligned between the micro-map and the expanded map.
Preserve banked frames across damage, retry, exit, and a partner leaving.
invariants: One film identity maps to one timeline arm per swimmer. A frame keeps its source identity even when it is reordered in a cut.
Screen-right and screen-up input move the swimmer in those directions in every controllable camera pose.
Opening the map, entering Focus, and changing the playback format preserve the current position or timestamp relevant to that action.
Predators announce danger before contact. A player can identify and take an escape route without sacrificing banked work.
mistake_conditions: The bell or gathered arms fill the viewport and hide the next passage.
The camera rolls, clips into the tube, or keeps retreating while the player tries to turn.
A fork becomes two decorative openings that lead to the same encounters.
A film appears as a hard-edged moving rectangle during the swim or screening.
The anglerfish lure reads exactly like a collectible, or a chase starts outside the visible approach.
Ending the dive leaves the swimmer drifting indefinitely with no result or exit.

mutable_variables: Current strength, recirculation, silt density, film brightness, time-slice spacing, and the location of animal crossings.
Which film lights the bell, which arm is pulled by drag, and how each recovered sequence trails into the water.
Whether a fork favors a quiet viewing pocket, a faster collecting route, or a hazardous passage with an optional rare frame.
atmospheric_range: Near-black teal water with soft silt and amber light.
A pale quiet pocket where the film expands in the water and the swimmer can hold position.
A short rust-red disturbance with broken frame order, followed by clear silhouettes and a readable exit.
surface_detail_range: Use refracted pinpoints, soft wake ribbons, blurred recesses, and light on the bell rim.
Blend each branch mouth into the surrounding volume. Let a contour emerge from silt and disappear gradually into the wall.
Keep a readable near field around the swimmer and current route markers. Increase haze and blur with depth.
transformation_range: A source frame condenses from drifting flecks into readable motion.
A recovered frame travels from the contacting arm into the bell, then appears in its film's trailing sequence.
The anglerfish lure concentrates light into a narrow pulse, then the body resolves behind it before the chase.
camera_variation_range: Default to a trailing three-quarter view with room ahead. Ease the look-ahead toward the next bend without moving the jelly to the edge of frame.
During Look or a slow film approach, arc laterally up to roughly 35 degrees, preserve camera clearance, and keep the route in view. Return along the same arc.
During Focus, shift clarity toward the side film gradually. Preserve sharp silhouettes for the jelly, nearby obstacles, and the next route opening.
Use wider framing for a ray crossing or partner approach. Bring the composition back to the player once the encounter passes.
permitted_drift: Shuffle background shoals, silt eddies, and minor film fragments inside a stable branch layout.
Allow density to build at a meaningful moment and release into dark water.
Let solo and partner dives produce different combinations of frames while retaining the same exit and provenance rules.
forbidden_drift: Persistent saturation, hard-edged HUD slabs, continuous camera orbit, and particles thick enough to hide steering cues.
Path commitments that occur before the player can read a mouth.
Creature attacks that permanently remove recovered work or force multiplayer participation.

diegesis.premise: The archive is a living system of connected currents. Each film occupies a stretch of water, and its earlier instants can be seen receding into depth.
world_rules: The main current carries the swimmer forward. Quiet eddies slow it enough to watch, orient, or recover control.
An expanded map shows explored chambers, the way back, and routes to the surface. A small edge map shows only the current reach and the next decision.
Living creatures move on their own clocks. Their wakes matter mechanically as well as visually.
Capture is a deliberate act of reaching. Watching a film leaves it available to revisit.
core_entities: Amber jelly swimmer with filmstock arms
Gaussian film clouds and timeworm sequences
Comb jellies, shrimp shoals, gliding rays, and an anglerfish
Contaminated fragments with distinct interference and warning marks
Optional second swimmer and explicitly shared frames
core_locations: A fork between a quiet film alcove and a fast channel
The surface chamber and Screening Room
dominant_relations: Current carries body and particles, while drag makes the arms follow with a delay.
A side encounter offers a choice to watch, capture, or pass.
A creature's wake changes which route or moment is easiest to reach.
A dive yields an editable sequence with provenance and a return path.

macro_units.function: Teach drift and scale through a playable opening.
macro_units.riverbed_role: Establish the stable steering view and the relation between swimmer, current, and film.
macro_units.flow_behavior: Sparse silt shows forward motion before the first film emerges at the side.

beats.shift: The player leaves the main axis to examine a side film.
beats.transition_channel: Lateral camera arc and gradual focus pull.
beats.prompt_burden: Keep the next passage visible while making the side encounter worth looking at.

patches.local_event: A face and raised hand gather from pale flecks. The swimmer uses Look, then releases it and resumes drift.
patches.camera_environment: Trailing three-quarter view easing toward profile with the same horizon.
patches.local_seed: Hold dark water around the small amber jelly. Let the hand resolve first, then the face. Move the camera only far enough to see film, swimmer, and onward water together.

macro_units.function: Make route choice legible and consequential.
macro_units.riverbed_role: Bind the map to actual passages and future film material.
macro_units.flow_behavior: The current separates into a quiet bend and a stronger open stream.

beats.shift: Two routes become readable before either takes hold.
beats.transition_channel: Continuous divergence, with the map revealing the fork in place.
beats.prompt_burden: Let the player understand where to go, why it matters, and when the choice commits.

patches.local_event: One mouth shows a quiet screening. A ray crosses the other and pulls a visible wake into the fast route.
patches.camera_environment: Wide trailing frame with both mouths clear and the local fork on the edge map.
what_must_hold: The map marks the selected throat
what_may_vary: Whether the player opens the expanded map
patches.local_seed: Split the particle flow before widening the walls. Give the quiet mouth slower suspended light and the fast mouth a readable pull. Let the swimmer choose by moving.

macro_units.function: Make danger, detours, and cooperation legible through motion.
macro_units.riverbed_role: Test navigation under pressure while preserving agency and recovered work.
macro_units.flow_behavior: A shrimp shoal scatters, the anglerfish reveals itself, and one escape current remains clean.

beats.shift: An apparent light source becomes a readable predator encounter.
beats.transition_channel: Local darkness lifts around the silhouette, followed by a bounded pursuit and release.
beats.prompt_burden: Teach the warning sequence before asking for evasive steering.

patches.local_event: A lure pulses twice. Shrimp peel away before the anglerfish turns. A solo swimmer takes the escape eddy, or a partner illuminates it from the side.
patches.camera_environment: Widen slightly and retain the jelly, predator silhouette, and escape mouth in the same view.
what_must_hold: The chase ends outside the predator pocket
what_may_vary: Whether the player risks a rare frame
patches.local_seed: Make the lure's paired pulse different from archive light. Reveal the body through its displacement of silt. Clear particles along the escape eddy before the predator moves.

macro_units.function: Give the dive a definitive end and a place to watch its result.
macro_units.riverbed_role: Convert traversal into an editable, watchable memory.
macro_units.flow_behavior: Current falls away, the arms settle into readable sequences, and the recovered cut becomes the focus.

beats.shift: Movement through the archive becomes playback of the recovered material.
beats.transition_channel: Continuous arrival, then optical match from filmstock to screening volume.
beats.prompt_burden: Make completion unmistakable and keep replay optional.

patches.local_event: Cross the surface threshold. Show recovered films, frames, and the route taken. Offer Watch cut, Edit cut, and Leave.
patches.camera_environment: Decelerate into a still side composition with the bell and arms inside the frame.
what_may_vary: Whether the cut contains any frames
Whether one or two swimmers arrive
Which optical format opens in the Screening Room
patches.local_seed: Remove propulsion and let the last wake pass. Match one visible frame in an arm to its first appearance in the Screening Room. Give an empty dive a clean exit and a route record.

prompt_architecture.master_prompt_strategy: Generate one continuous playable route with a real fork, a quiet side screening, a predator pocket, and a marked surface. Establish steering, framing, and archive identity before increasing ecological density.
prompt_architecture.continuity_law: Carry swimmer position, heading, arm ownership, film identity, timestamps, and route history across camera moves, branches, viewing modes, and completion.
prompt_architecture.style_law: Use the contact sheet's scale and restraint. Keep the amber swimmer small against teal-black water. Give the film room to emerge beside it. Reserve intense bloom and red contamination for brief events, then let the image clear.
prompt_architecture.transition_law: Show every consequential change through a readable precursor, contact or crossing, and aftermath. A branch pulls before it commits. A film resolves before it can be gathered. A predator telegraphs before it pursues. The surface decelerates the swimmer before presenting the cut.
negative_constraints: No close chase shot that crops the swimmer or hides its escape direction.
No flat moving video rectangles or frame-filling fault effects.
No camera roll during steering, instant camera flips, unmarked dead ends, or irreversible route switches before a threshold.
No generic hostile shoals. Give each creature a recognizable motion and a specific local effect.
No mandatory partner, shared-camera tugging, duplicate capture awards, or loss of work when a partner disconnects.
prompt_architecture.master_prompt: Build the archive as navigable water with a readable current and a continuously framed, small amber swimmer. Give the player separate controls for steering, looking, focusing, and casting. Let soft film volumes emerge beside the route and preserve their source clocks through watching and capture. Split the current into a genuine choice between distinct encounters, preview both mouths on the micro-map, and update the chosen path only after crossing. Populate the route with animals whose motion changes the water, and stage the anglerfish through warning, visible pursuit, and a reachable escape. Grow one trailing timeline for each newly captured film and add subsequent source frames to that arm. At the surface, bank the material, show the route taken, and let the swimmer watch, edit, or leave.

segment_prompts.purpose: Tune the playable camera and controls first.
segment_prompts.prompt: Validate a level trailing view in portrait and landscape during neutral drift, sustained steering into a wall, Focus, and Look. Keep the next opening visible. Give input a small dead zone, limit acceleration, damp release, and project wall contact along the surface. Use a camera collision check and bounded follow distance so neither the body nor the camera can remain wedged.

segment_prompts.purpose: Build a useful fork and map.
segment_prompts.prompt: Connect two smooth passages that offer different films, current speeds, and animal encounters. Place a micro-map at an edge with the player, two upcoming mouths, and the next safe rejoin. Expand it on demand to show discovered routes and the surface. Use matching symbols in the water and on the map, and communicate a committed branch by changing the traced route.

Use comb jellies as visible current tracers, shrimp as an early disturbance cue, and a ray as a moving broad wake. Give the anglerfish a bounded patrol, a distinct two-pulse lure, and a short pursuit. Put a safe eddy within the player's view before the pursuit starts. An optional risky frame may sit near the lure, while the main route remains clear.

Prototype two independently steered swimmers with local cameras and map markers. Give each a personal collection and explicit frame sharing. In online play, validate capture IDs once at the session authority and reconcile state after reconnect. A departing swimmer leaves the route and banked collections usable. Keep all navigation, viewing, capture, and exit actions available to a solo swimmer.

segment_prompts.purpose: Close the loop from swimming to filmmaking.
segment_prompts.prompt: At the surface, stop forward drift, bank recovered frames, and show the traveled route with the resulting cut. Let the player watch it as splats or timeworms, edit it, or swim a new route in its cut order. On a failed dive, retain banked material and offer the last safe rejoin or the Screening Room.

bridge_prompts.function: Reveal a film without losing orientation.
bridge_prompts.prompt: Slow the camera arc as the film comes into focus. Keep a piece of the forward tube in view and retain the swimmer on the near edge of the composition. On release, return at the same rate and preserve heading.

bridge_prompts.function: Make a voluntary route commitment visible.
bridge_prompts.prompt: Show divergent particle streams and both map mouths before crossing. After the swimmer enters one throat, emphasize its current and trace the committed route. Leave a downstream rejoin visible on the expanded map.

bridge_prompts.function: Show the captured image becoming anatomy.
bridge_prompts.prompt: Keep the contact point visible while flecks travel into the bell. Unfurl a short arm for a new film. For a known film, add the frame at its source position and lengthen that arm. Let the wake carry older stock behind the current steering view.

bridge_prompts.function: End locomotion and preserve the recovered sequence.
bridge_prompts.prompt: Let the current fall quiet and settle the camera. Show the route and recovered material once. Open playback at the chosen frame and retain its timestamp when switching formats. Leave the swimmer free to exit.

constraint_prompts.prompt: Test a nearly empty jelly and one with many timeline arms. Keep the bell scale consistent, place trailing arms in depth, and preserve the approach corridor in both aspect ratios. Prioritize a readable path when a film, predator, and accumulated arms share the frame.

constraint_prompts.purpose: Keep route and film state coherent.
constraint_prompts.prompt: Verify both branches, the return eddy, map reopen, and the route trace at completion. For each captured frame, verify matching film ID and timestamp in the arm, the cut, the Screening Room, and the cut rebuilt as a route.

Test simultaneous contact with one frame, a deliberate share, a disconnect during an encounter, and solo completion of the same route. Keep each swimmer's camera and steering independent and record each valid capture once.

model_behavior_priority: Prove the swim camera and steering in a sparse tube before adding creatures or glow.
Make one fork, its map, and the rejoin work end to end.
Add one ecological encounter whose wake changes a route choice.
Verify capture, arm growth, surface completion, and screening in solo play before introducing a second swimmer.
stability_targets: At rest and during wall contact, the swimmer remains in frame and can resume forward movement.
Side viewing returns smoothly to the same steering composition.
The next fork is visible before commitment in both portrait and landscape.
A late dive with many arms remains readable during a hazard.
A failed or empty dive still reaches a clear recovery or exit state.
controlled_variability_targets: Vary available films, minor animal crossings, and local current strength while retaining the same branch affordances.
Vary the visual density of splats and slices while retaining recognizable subject, source time, and playback position.
Allow players to travel separately and rejoin without synchronizing their cameras or sacrificing either collection.
failure_risks: Adding ecology before camera and steering are stable turns the tube into visual noise.
Using depth blur on navigation cues makes a cinematic frame difficult to play.
Unbounded arm length recreates the crowded reference fault.
A map that reports every moving creature becomes another obstruction.
Multiplayer state that treats capture as a visual effect instead of a recorded event can duplicate or lose frames.
